title: The Red Sticker
premise_public: A courier arrived with a sealed package in perfect condition. A small square on its label had turned red, so she refused to hand it over. The recipient thanked her.
solution_summary: The square was a temperature-exposure indicator. It turned red because a cold-chain delivery containing refrigerated medication had warmed too much to be trusted as safe or effective.

facts.text: The package contained medication requiring refrigerated transport.
The square on its label was a temperature-exposure indicator.
The indicator had turned red after the safe temperature limit was exceeded.
The contents could no longer be trusted as safe or effective.
The sealed packaging had not been deliberately tampered with.

acceptable_solutions: The red square was a temperature indicator showing refrigerated medicine had warmed up.
The cold-chain temperature sticker warned that the medication inside might be spoiled.
It was a temperature-sensitive drug shipment, and its indicator showed unsafe warmth.
hints: A perfect seal cannot guarantee the contents are usable.
The label might reveal a condition you cannot see inside.
